themes_detail.label: Encampment surge in Bed-Stuy
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 10 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score 4.56), signaling a rapid deterioration in street-level homelessness that aligns with recurring community board requests for expanded homeless services.
evidence: 10 encampment complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 average per week over prior 8 weeks
700% spike represents highest z-score anomaly (4.56) among current active spikes
Community board has repeatedly requested 'other services for the homeless' from Department of Homeless Services, suggesting this is a persistent, now-accelerating problem
reporting_angles: Why are encampments growing now? Interview DHS, local precinct, and affected residents about triggers and timeline
Where are encampments concentrating? Map the 10 complaints to identify hotspots (transit hubs, parks, commercial corridors)

themes_detail.label: Building maintenance crisis escalating
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints jumped to 27 THIS WEEK versus 7.4 weekly average (266% spike, z-score 4.87), suggesting a sudden wave of building system failures or neglect affecting residential and commercial properties across the district.
evidence: 27 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
266% spike with z-score 4.87 indicates statistically significant deviation
Complements existing high volume of heat/hot water (3465 complaints over 90 days) and plumbing complaints (735), suggesting systemic building infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: What types of maintenance failures are driving the spike? Analyze complaint categories (HVAC, electrical, structural, etc.) to identify pattern
Are landlords deferring maintenance? Cross-reference with housing court filings and HPD violations to assess compliance trends

themes_detail.label: Drug activity spike in district
themes_detail.summary: Drug Activity complaints rose to 7 LAST WEEK versus 1.5 weekly average (367% increase, z-score 3.89), indicating a concentrated emergence of open drug use or dealing that warrants immediate community safety investigation.
evidence: 7 drug activity complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
367% spike with z-score 3.89 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Correlates with 300% spike in non-emergency police matters (16 complaints 3 weeks ago vs 4.0 avg), suggesting broader public safety stress
reporting_angles: Where are complaints concentrated geographically? Map the 7 incidents to identify drug markets or trafficking corridors
Is this connected to supply chain changes, turf shifts, or reduced enforcement? Interview NYPD, community stakeholders, and outreach workers

themes_detail.label: Food safety concerns emerging
themes_detail.summary: Food Poisoning complaints jumped to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score 4.85), potentially signaling a cluster contamination event or pattern of unsafe food handling at local restaurants or vendors.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
540% spike with z-score 4.85 represents second-highest severity anomaly
Community board has recurring request to 'increase health and safety inspections for restaurants and childcare programs,' indicating baseline capacity concerns at DOHMH
reporting_angles: Is this a cluster from one venue or distributed across multiple locations? Request DOH inspection data and complaint-sourcing from 311
Are restaurants operating with reduced staffing or cut-rate suppliers? Interview affected residents and check DOH violation records

themes_detail.label: Street sanitation and lot deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot Condition complaints spiked to 7 THREE WEEKS AGO (600% increase, z-score 4.24) alongside elevated Dumpster Complaints (5 complaints, 471% spike), reflecting rapid accumulation of debris, illegal dumping, or neglected vacant properties across Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 7 lot condition complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 1.0 weekly average (600% spike, z-score 4.24)
5 dumpster complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 0.9 weekly average (471% spike, z-score 5.28)
Combined with baseline 905 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days, suggests systemic sanitation management breakdown in specific neighborhoods
reporting_angles: Map the 7 lot complaints to identify neighborhoods with chronic dumping or neglect; investigate property ownership and code enforcement history
Is this tied to construction activity or reduced street sweeping? Cross-reference with DOB permits and DSNY scheduling data
